study.question: Does chronological adjacency between DIFFERENT action types within a target-category/brand matching subsequence add useful joint history-field evidence beyond the incumbent per-action match states and action composition?
study.hypothesis: The parent partitions sequence summaries by action before constructing switches/endpoints, so no feature explicitly records chronological cross-action adjacency within one target-field subsequence. R0031 match/nonmatch contrast fell below its persistence controls; only629/4096 field/action coordinates had common support and187/629 were sparse in the candidate-supplied first512 diagnostics. These motivate changing the represented state space rather than another within-action persistence transform. Pool all action types into each field-matched timestamp sequence, retain the four-action distribution of tied events, and expose 12 directed off-diagonal older-to-newer joint rates per field. If useful information lies in cross-action ordering conditional on a coarse target field, target_ordered should beat target_exchangeable and show a positive order-by-population interaction. This is a prospective representation hypothesis, not a purchase funnel or causal mechanism claim.

nearest_work.difference: DIN section4.3 describes target-aware weighted pooling, unnormalized intensity, and limitations of generic sequence modeling. We inherit the local field-adapted activation ancestry (which uses softmax, unlike original DIN), with the current blind query frozen. New contrast is a deterministic field-matched chronological four-action adjacency readout versus an analytic group-permutation null. No original-priority claim; broad multi-behavior/Markov-statistic novelty is unverified.

Author README verifies category/brand/action histories lack item IDs. Our transitions join only coarse target fields; never infer an item trajectory. Publisher paper not accessible, DIEN not a registered authorized source, so no full DMR/DIEN equivalence or superiority claim.

Whole incumbent source matches authorized receipt hash. It groups each field separately within action and adds match-state switches/newest endpoints. R0031 additionally contrasts match persistence with return. Proposed addon changes to action identities as states after field matching and includes cross-action off-diagonal adjacency; complete incumbent retained.

inherited_components: All incumbent embeddings, action/age encodings, blind shared relevance attention and MLP; no optimizer/loss changes
All count, decay, support, rank, extrema, anchor, frontier, newer-count, same-action switch and latest-endpoint features from r0027-latest_endpoint
Raw-age sorting, timestamp tie fractions and exact group-permutation comparison idea from the local switch lineage; new four-action state calculation is an ordinary descriptive pair statistic
study.proposed_difference: Append24 zero-initialized classifier columns: category then brand, older action1..4/newer action1..4 excluding equal actions. For each field, target population=positive-ID target matches across all known actions; activity=all positive-ID field events. Both require known positive target ID. Collapse each raw timestamp to a four-action probability vector p_g, sorted newest first. Observed older->newer matrix=sum_g p_(g+1) outer p_g /(G-1). Exact uniform timestamp-group permutation mean=(S outer S-sum_g p_g outer p_g)/(G*(G-1)). Gate all cells on target and activity having>=2 groups and use half-scale. All4 tables executed in every cell. Target subsequence skips nonmatches, whereas activity subsequence retains them; this is part of the population intervention, not controlled original-stream adjacency.
predictions: Primary: target_ordered AUC minus target_exchangeable AUC >0, alongside target_ordered exceeding r0027-latest_endpoint AUC0.6208079251798616; improvement under.0001 is practically weak pending repetitions.

Factorial: (target_ordered-target_exchangeable)-(activity_ordered-activity_exchangeable)>0 would provisionally favor target-conditioned cross-action chronology rather than global action ordering. Analyze AUC and Logloss separately, not an unregistered combined score.

First512 label-blind diagnostics should show positive common/multi-action support, nonzero target cross-action rates, finite logits/features, null symmetry and near-zero group/event/mass/parent identity errors. If support is negligible, interpretation is an unavailable-evidence limitation rather than a refutation.

Existing host slices by history length, behavior composition, hour and user training-frequency are exploratory with supplied sample/positive/negative counts. Sparse/empty-history and missing-target feature values remain zero; trained shared weights can still change their logits.
falsifiers: No AUC advantage over target_exchangeable weakens utility of chronological cross-action order under this recipe, even if both beat the smaller incumbent.
No target-specific interaction or activity_ordered matching/beating target_ordered weakens the proposed target-field linkage; field-independent action composition/chronology may suffice.

No improvement over incumbent, worse unweighted Logloss, or gains below seed variation prevents selecting or asserting a robust improvement. One trial does not establish or refute the broad mechanism.

Zero/rare supported multi-action target subsequences, nonfinite diagnostics, reversed older/newer implementation, nonzero unsupported extras, or identity errors beyond float32 rounding invalidate interpretation and require a charged corrective host run before conclusions.
alternative_explanations: Additional24 classifier columns add3072 parameters and change optimization/regularization; all4 cells capacity/RNG matched, historical incumbent is smaller.
Target vs activity changes group counts, tie compositions and which events are neighbors; common support removes eligibility differences but not these intrinsic population differences.
Joint normalization includes repeat-action pairs in G-1 even though only cross-action entries are supplied, so summary mass also reflects diversity and event recency truncation.
Behavioral associations may be user activity or category popularity rather than intent; hashed IDs and coarse fields do not identify items or establish causality.

Extensive adaptive seed42 validation search and best-checkpoint selection can overfit validation; first512 diagnostics are nonrepresentative and candidate-supplied. Need frozen paired seeds and user-cluster uncertainty where host permits.
